svg.aria-label: Antibiotic use and resistance. This diagram gives no doses; if a doctor can be reached, any suspected bacterial infection should be seen by a doctor first, not treated from your stock of drugs; there is no reliable way to make antibiotics at home, this handbook gives none, so stock finished drugs and focus on prevention. 1, antibiotics work only on bacterial infections: pus in a wound, high fever for more than 3 days, local redness, swelling, heat and pain, and a raised white cell count suggest bacterial infection, but a doctor must judge; this is not a reason to self-medicate; do not use them for viral infections (colds, flu), for preventive use, or for fever of unknown cause; they have no effect on viruses, fungi or parasites. 2, resistance is natural selection: during treatment most bacteria are killed, a few that are naturally unaffected by the drug survive, the survivors multiply, and the same drug no longer works next time; resistant bacteria also spread among family and neighbours, and after a collapse there is no sensitivity testing and no new drug to switch to. 3, what speeds up resistance: antibiotics for viral infections, stopping as soon as you feel better, on-and-off use, cutting the dose yourself, splitting one course among several people, taking other people's leftovers or drugs of unknown origin, and preventive use without a reason. 4, the right way: one drug at a time, never combine drugs on your own; full dose and full course as prescribed, do not stop as soon as you feel better; if there is no improvement at all after 2-3 days, or it gets worse, see a doctor as soon as possible, do not switch or add drugs yourself; keep the original pack and leaflet and check contraindications and allergy history; record the drug name, the time of each dose and the temperature every day. 5, during treatment: local rash or itching, stop and contact a doctor; a rash with blisters, peeling skin, or sores in the mouth or eyes, stop and call 120; a tight throat, difficulty breathing, swollen face or lips, dizziness and collapse are anaphylactic shock, treat as in 1.3 and call 120; frequent diarrhoea, blood or mucus, abdominal pain and fever, stop and see a doctor now; yellow skin or whites of the eyes, urine as dark as strong tea, or much less urine, stop and see a doctor as soon as possible. Prevention is far better than cure
svg.title: Antibiotic use and resistance

g.text: Antibiotics: they work only on bacteria; use every tablet right
⚠ This diagram gives no doses. If a doctor can be reached, any suspected bacterial
infection should be seen by a doctor first, not treated from your stock of drugs.
There is no reliable way to make antibiotics at home, and this handbook gives none.
Stock finished drugs, keep the leaflets, and focus on prevention.
① When to use: only for bacterial infections
bacterium
✓ Signs of bacterial infection
· Pus in a wound
· High fever for more than 3 days
· Local redness, swelling, heat, pain
· Raised white cell count
(if it can be tested)
A doctor must judge; this is not a reason
to take drugs on your own
virus
✗ Do not use for
· Viral infections (colds, flu)
· Preventive use
(wasteful, and breeds resistance)
· Fever of unknown cause
· No effect on viruses, fungi
or parasites
A common cold is mostly runny nose and sore
throat, and clears up by itself in about a week
② How resistance arises: natural selection
Before treatment
During treatment
Afterwards
drug
multiply
Most bacteria are killed by this drug;
a few (red) are naturally unaffected
Most are killed;
the unaffected ones survive
The survivors multiply;
the same drug no longer works
⚠ Resistant bacteria also spread among family and neighbours; after a collapse
there is no sensitivity testing and no new drug to switch to
③ These speed up resistance
✗ Antibiotics for colds, flu or other viruses
✗ Stopping once you feel better, on-and-off
use, cutting the dose yourself
✗ Splitting one course among several people
✗ Taking other people's leftovers or drugs
of unknown origin
✗ “Preventive” use without a reason
Once resistant bacteria appear in a community,
your stock has in effect lost a class of drug
④ The right way
✓ One drug at a time; never combine on your own
✓ Full dose and full course as prescribed;
don't stop as soon as you feel better
✓ No improvement at all after 2-3 days, or worse
→ see a doctor as soon as possible;
don't switch or add drugs yourself
✓ Keep the original pack and leaflet; check
contraindications and allergy history
✓ Record drug name, dose times, daily temperature
⑤ If any of these appear during treatment: stop the drug
Local rash, itching
Rash with blisters, peeling skin,
sores in the mouth or eyes
Tight throat, difficulty breathing,
swollen face or lips, dizziness, collapse
Frequent diarrhoea, blood or mucus,
abdominal pain with fever
Yellow skin or eyes, urine dark as strong tea,
much less urine
Stop; contact a doctor; note the drug name
Stop; call 120 now (severe drug rash)
Anaphylactic shock: treat as in 1.3; call 120
Stop; see a doctor now; guard against dehydration
Liver/kidney damage: stop; see a doctor soon
Prevention >> stocked finished drugs >> natural antibacterials (support only)
>> home-made (almost impossible)
Wash hands often, drink boiled water, irrigate wounds under pressure:
prevention is far better than cure
